summary: @nebula.js/sn-distributionplot 1.0.7 ships preinstall dropper that downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: This version of @nebula.js/sn-distributionplot declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs` in package.json. setup.mjs is an obfuscated loader (renamed `_0x...` identifiers, per-call string dictionaries) that downloads the Bun runtime from the oven-sh GitHub releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and then invokes it via execFileSync against a sibling file `math_init.js`. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line obfuscator.io-style bundle (rotating string array, hex-named identifiers, custom decoder) whose executed contents are not human-inspectable without decoding. Neither setup.mjs nor math_init.js is listed in the package.json `files` allowlist (which declares only api-specifications, core, core/esm, dist, sn-distributionplot-ext), yet both are shipped in the tarball and run at install time. The bundled dist/sn-distplot.js banner reads v1.0.6 while the package version is 1.0.7, and the legitimate upstream qlik-oss/nebula.js repository has no preinstall script or Bun dependency. The package repackages legitimate Qlik supernova bundle contents while smuggling in an undeclared, obfuscated payload executed under a freshly-downloaded alternate runtime — an alternate-runtime-dropper pattern designed to bypass Node-based scanners at `npm install` time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
